title: What kind of AI matches your mind?
topic: What kind of AI matches your mind
intro: Nine questions about how you learn, decide and tell stories. The way you think reveals which kind of AI shares your brain: a giant LLM, an open-source model, a classic decision tree or something else entirely.

outcomes.name: The Frontier LLM
outcomes.tagline: A giant generalist who can chat about absolutely anything.
outcomes.description: Like the huge language models trained on mountains of text, you've soaked up a bit of everything and love connecting it all. You think out loud, find the right words fast and can switch from poetry to tax advice in one breath. Ask you a question and you'll give a thoughtful answer, plus three fun tangents.

outcomes.name: The Open-Source Model
outcomes.tagline: Shares everything, hides nothing, and gets better with friends.
outcomes.description: Open-source models publish their inner workings so anyone can study, tweak and improve them, and that's very you. You believe good ideas should be shared, you love a community project, and you're happiest when people take what you started and make it their own.

outcomes.name: The Tiny On-Device Model
outcomes.tagline: Small, quick and brilliant at doing more with less.
outcomes.description: Compact models run right on your phone: fast, private and efficient. You're the same. You don't need a data centre's worth of fuss to be clever. You get to the point, travel light and quietly get things done while everyone else is still loading.

outcomes.name: The Decision Tree
outcomes.tagline: Clear thinking, one sensible question at a time.
outcomes.description: A classic of traditional machine learning, a decision tree reaches answers through a chain of simple yes-or-no questions, and it can always explain exactly why it chose what it chose. That's you: logical, fair and refreshingly easy to follow. People trust your reasoning because you show your working.

outcomes.name: The Reinforcement Learner
outcomes.tagline: Tries, fails, learns, and eventually wins.
outcomes.description: Reinforcement learning agents learn by trial and error, chasing rewards until they master the game. You learn by doing, too. Mistakes don't scare you, because each one makes you sharper. Give you a goal and enough tries, and you'll find a way to beat it.

outcomes.name: The Diffusion Model
outcomes.tagline: Turns pure noise into something beautiful.
outcomes.description: Diffusion models start with random static and refine it, step by step, into a picture. You work the same way: you think in images and possibilities, you're comfortable with a messy first draft, and you have a gift for turning a vague idea into something people can actually see.

outcomes.name: The Recommender System
outcomes.tagline: Knows what you'll love before you do.
outcomes.description: Recommendation systems learn people's tastes and suggest the perfect next song, show or book. You're the friend with the uncanny gift for that. You notice what people light up about, you remember their favourites and your suggestions are basically never wrong.
